plan.title: README 'Cold-start bootstrap (read this first)' block contradicts the learner pin boundary taught in Module 2

narratives.Description: The byte-zero managed cold-start block is labeled read-this-first and currently reaches `directive doctor` and a global install before any learner-only guidance, contradicting the disposable pin boundary taught later in the course. This story inserts a learner audience intercept inside that managed block while preserving the agent bootstrap ladder and locking the distinction in focused portability checks.
narratives.ImplementationPlan:
1. Update the managed cold-start block in `README.md` with an in-block, learner-prefixed audience intercept before any learner could follow the doctor or global-install rungs, while retaining the byte-zero marker and agent ladder.
2. Keep `curriculum/README.md` consistent with the disposable project-local pin boundary without adding a global Directive prerequisite or a new `START-HERE.md` route.
3. Extend `scripts/verify-cold-start-readme.mjs` and its `scripts/verify-text-portability.test.mjs` mutations so LF and CRLF evidence rejects removal, after-title placement, or loss of the learner identity gate.
narratives.UserStory: As a course learner, I want the first README block to identify which instructions are only for maintainers and agents, so that I do not run global or repository-mutating bootstrap commands before starting the disposable course path.
narratives.Traces: GitHub issue #94 and its ingested design-critique Bound remedy require an in-block learner intercept, preserve the byte-zero agent ladder, and bind focused cold-start plus text-portability verification while excluding a new learner entry file.
narratives.Overview:
- The managed cold-start heading is titled "(agents and maintainers)" and the intercepting Learners skip sentence is "**Learners:** skip this block." Byte 0 stays the #2273 agent ladder.
- The bound Learners audience line is "**Learners:** skip this block" and sends learners to a "project-local graph" in a "disposable repository".
- The focused cold-start verifier requires "the cold-start block must contain a Learners-prefixed audience line" and "the Learners audience line must keep the skip-sentence identity".
- The course map still says "Do not install or initialize lab tooling in this training" and "Each lab that changes files supplies a disposable starting" and does not add START-HERE.md.

Stop 1 identity: one learner skip sentence after `# directive-training` and before `## Start here`. P1's named learner path is following the README's first heading, "read this first", through rung 1 and rung 3.

## 1. The skip has to intercept the first heading

class: blocks-the-design

Evidence, re-measured at `aea1e770`:

- `README.md:2` titles the managed block "Cold-start bootstrap (read this first)".
- `README.md:6` rung 1: a running `directive doctor` means the reader is bootstrapped and should follow `Next command:`.
- `README.md:8` rung 3: `npm i -g @deftai/directive@0.119.5`.
- `labs/02-disposable-initialization.md:81` and `:231` tell the learner never to accept a host-global binary. `curriculum/modules/02-installation-and-anatomy.md:232-233` classifies `npm i -g` as outside the disposable boundary.
- `node scripts/verify-cold-start-readme.mjs` on a SHA snapshot prints `README cold-start bootstrap: ok`.
- The same verifier on mutated `/tmp` READMEs: a skip before byte 0 fails (`the cold-start marker must begin at byte 0`); a skip between the close marker and the title fails (`the project title must immediately follow the closing marker`); a skip after the title passes; a Learners audience line inside the managed block passes; retitling the first heading inside the block passes.
- `README.md:21-22`, already after the title, says this repository is the course source and also a Directive consumer. That is the after-title identity prose the reporter still had to reason past.

Failure mode: the harvest lands a skip between the title and `## Start here`. The first imperative on the page still sends a learner through `directive doctor` and `npm i -g` before that skip. That is the path P1 names and the reporter ran.

Disposition: this recut cannot bind with after-title placement. Keep the skip-sentence identity. Put the intercepting line inside the managed block: a Learners-prefixed audience line, a retitle of "read this first", or both. The existing cold-start verifier already accepts those edits. Byte 0 stays the #2273 agent ladder. The harvest stays on `README.md`.

## 2. "Learners" on that sentence is load-bearing

class: sharpens-framing

Evidence: `.deft/core/packs/rules/rules-pack-0.1.json` `main-002` requires agents to follow the README cold-start block before any other instruction. Completed issue 2 placed that block at byte 0 so AGENTS.md recovery still works when `.deft/core/` is missing.

Failure mode: harvest text that says "skip this block" with no audience gate. Agents recovering from README then skip the ladder that `main-002` and #2273 require.

Disposition: the bound sentence names learners, or an equivalent audience gate. Agents keep the global-first ladder.

## 3. Lock the intercepting line on the existing verifier

class: sharpens-framing

Evidence: `scripts/verify-cold-start-readme.mjs` locks byte 0, title adjacency, rungs 1–6, and the pinned rung-3 commands. `scripts/verify-text-portability.test.mjs` already spawns that verifier under LF and CRLF, including a separated-title mutation. Neither asserts an audience line. `assertTeachingBaselinePin` still returns `0.119.5` with a skip inserted after the title in `/tmp`.

Failure mode: the next managed-block refresh or README edit drops the audience line and CI stays green.

Disposition: extend `scripts/verify-cold-start-readme.mjs` and the existing portability mutations that already call it.

## 4. Course map and START-HERE.md

class: footnote

`curriculum/README.md` prerequisites list Node, Git, gh, npm, Task, uv, Python, and a coding-agent host. They already omit a global `directive`. `START-HERE.md` is absent at this SHA. Those two issue-body branches already match the tree; the recut left them out.

## Existing mechanism inventory

- Managed block plus `scripts/verify-cold-start-readme.mjs` (byte 0, title adjacency, rung pin). In-block prose is already a legal edit; issue 63 already edited rung 3 inside the same markers.
- Teaching-baseline HTML comments around `0.119.5` under `## Start here`.
- `README.md:21-22` consumer-versus-course identity, after the title.
- `## Safety boundary` at `README.md:72`, after Start here, too late for "read this first".
- Lab 2 runtime refusal and Module 2 `npm i -g` boundary, which teach the rule after the README has already offered the opposite command.
- `main-002` agent recovery through this same README block.

## Injection / identity lens

The target changes reader identity on shared README state: agents take the #2273 ladder; learners skip it. An unscoped skip is a prompt collision with `main-002`. The deterministic control is an audience-gated line inside the block the first heading names, locked by the existing verifier.

## Road not taken

After-title skip keeps the managed ladder byte-for-byte for agents and survives a later rewrite of the marked block. That is the strongest case for the recut placement. It flips when the first heading is an imperative the learner executes before the title, which is the report on this issue.

metadata.issueBody:
## Course context

I noticed this as a mid/senior learner. The pre-check before Module 1 found a global `directive` **0.119.9** on my `PATH`, while the course pins **0.119.5**. The machine runs Windows 11 ARM64 and PowerShell 7.6.6.

## What happened

The first thing on `README.md` is a callout titled **"⚡ Cold-start bootstrap (read this first)"**. It says:

1. "**Already installed?** Run `directive doctor` ... If it runs, you're bootstrapped — skip the rest and follow its `Next command:`."
2. "**Global install (canonical).** `npm i -g @deftai/directive@0.119.5` ..."

That block is Directive-managed bootstrap guidance for agents working **in this repository** (the maintainer workspace). Nothing marks it as not for learners. It is followed by `## Start here`, which is the learner path.

The block contradicts what the course teaches:

- Rung 1 tells a learner with **any** global version that they are "bootstrapped". Module 2 and Lab 2 teach that a host-global executable never proves the pin ("never accept a host-global binary instead").
- Rung 3 calls a host-global install canonical. Module 2 (§4) and Lab 2 Task 2 teach learners to **refuse** `npm i -g` because it mutates host-global state outside the disposable boundary.
- "Follow its `Next command:`" invites learners to act on doctor's recommendations in the training repository. That repository is the one place the course says never to run Directive commands.

## Learner pain

A learner who does what the page says, "read this first", before "Start here", will either:

- run `directive doctor` in the curriculum clone and act on its next command, which mutates the training repo; or
- run `npm i -g @deftai/directive@0.119.5`, which downgrades or changes their global tool. Module 2 later calls that exact action outside the boundary.

For me, rung 1 would have declared a mismatched 0.119.9 install "bootstrapped". I had to reason out that the block was not for me, and that the labs install their own exact project-local graph.

## Reproduction

1. Open `README.md` with a global `directive` of a different version installed.
2. Follow the "read this first" block top-down.

## Proposed fix

- Add a sentence at the top of the managed block, or directly under it, before `## Start here`. For example: "**Learners:** skip this block. It is maintainer/agent bootstrap for this repository. You do not need a global `directive`; every lab installs its own exact project-local 0.119.5 graph in a disposable repository. Do not run Directive commands in this clone."
- In the course map's prerequisites, say whether a global `directive` is needed. As far as I can tell it is not. Also say that a global CLI of a different version is harmless but must not be used as lab evidence.
- If the managed block cannot be edited because the installer owns it, move the learner guidance above it or into a learner-only `START-HERE.md`.
